plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.

interactionPlan.concept: When the lower boundary of a plane region is given by two different formulas on either side of x = 0, the region must be split into two type-I sub-regions and the double integral written as a sum of two iterated integrals.
elements: Horizontal x-axis with arrow and label 'x', tick marks and labels at -2, 0, 2
Vertical y-axis with arrow and label 'y' (origin at intersection, y-axis drawn tall enough to reach above y = 3)
Triangular region with vertices (-2, 3), (0, 1), (2, 3) outlined in thick blue
Top boundary segment y = 3 from (-2,3) to (2,3), thick blue, with label 'y = 3' placed twice (above the left half and above the right half)
Lower-left boundary segment y = -x + 1 from (-2,3) to (0,1), thick blue, labeled 'y = -x + 1' to the left of the region
Lower-right boundary segment y = x + 1 from (0,1) to (2,3), thick blue, labeled 'y = x + 1' to the right of the region
Left sub-region R1 (x from -2 to 0) shaded pale blue with interior label 'R₁'
Right sub-region R2 (x from 0 to 2) shaded pale orange/yellow with interior label 'R₂'
Red vertical strip inside R1 at about x = -1, running from the lower boundary up to y = 3
Red vertical strip inside R2 at about x = 0.7, running from the lower boundary up to y = 3
Dashed vertical divider along the y-axis marking the split between R1 and R2
Iterated-integral readout panel showing ∫₋₂⁰∫_{-x+1}^{3} f dy dx + ∫₀²∫_{x+1}^{3} f dy dx
Small caption box showing the current lower-boundary formulas for each side

interactions.label: Lower boundary of each sub-region
interactions.teaches: The inner integral's lower limit IS the lower boundary formula; because that formula changes expression at x = 0, one single iterated integral cannot describe the whole region.

interactions.label: Vertical strip position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the red strip across the region shows the inner integral running from y = lower(x) up to y = 3, and shows the lower endpoint jumping formulas as the strip crosses x = 0.

interactions.label: Region view
interactions.teaches: Seeing R as one shape versus two colored halves makes clear that the split is a bookkeeping device for the limits, not a change to the region itself.

demo_steps.title: The region R
demo_steps.narration: R is the triangle bounded above by y = 3 and below by the two lines y = -x + 1 and y = x + 1, with vertices (-2, 3), (0, 1) and (2, 3).

demo_steps.title: A vertical strip on the left
demo_steps.narration: Fix x between -2 and 0. The red strip runs from the lower boundary y = -x + 1 up to y = 3, so the inner integral is ∫ from -x+1 to 3 dy.

demo_steps.title: Crossing x = 0
demo_steps.narration: Drag the strip past the y-axis: the top of the strip stays at y = 3, but the bottom suddenly follows y = x + 1 instead. The lower limit changes formula exactly at x = 0.

demo_steps.title: Two integrals, one region
demo_steps.narration: Because no single formula gives the bottom of every strip, R is written as R₁ ∪ R₂ and the double integral becomes ∫₋₂⁰∫_{-x+1}^{3} + ∫₀²∫_{x+1}^{3}.

demo_steps.title: Edit a boundary
demo_steps.narration: Type a new lower boundary for either half — say 'x^2 + 1' on the right. The blue curve, the shaded area, and the corresponding inner limit all update together, confirming that the limit is the boundary.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The inner limits of a type-I double integral are literally the upper and lower boundary curves; when the lower boundary switches formula at x = 0, you must switch integrals there too.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Centered coordinate axes in black with arrowheads, x-axis labeled at -2, 0, 2 and a tall y-axis. A downward-pointing triangle sits above the x-axis with vertices (-2,3), (0,1), (2,3), outlined in a thick medium-blue stroke. Left half (x<0) filled pale blue labeled R₁; right half filled pale peach/yellow labeled R₂; the y-axis acts as the divider. Labels 'y = 3' sit just above the top edge on both halves, 'y = -x + 1' outside the region to the left, 'y = x + 1' outside to the right, all in serif italic math style. Two thin red vertical segments inside the halves run from the slanted lower edge up to the top edge, representing inner integration in y. Keep generous whitespace; the whole triangle occupies the upper-middle of the canvas with the x-axis low. Add a small readout of the iterated integral sum below or beside the figure, updating live with the edited boundary expressions.

discrepancies: The generated figure adds a large readout panel below the axes (integral formula, computed areas, strip readout) that has no counterpart in the source; it occupies roughly a third of the canvas and shrinks the actual figure.
A dashed blue segment is drawn along the y-axis between y=1 and y=3 as a divider — not present in the source, where the two shaded halves simply abut.

The source shows two equally solid red vertical strips (one in R₁, one in R₂); the generated version draws the companion strip at 50% opacity, so the second strip reads as faint/secondary rather than as a peer annotation.

The '0' tick label is placed to the left of the y-axis (at x≈−0.24) whereas the source places it to the right of the axis, and tick marks are drawn above the axis rather than as the source's short crossing marks.

On load the step player reads 'Step 1 / 5 — The region R' (whose scripted state is the un-split whole region), yet the drawing shows the split R₁/R₂ view with the checkbox on — the narration and rendered state disagree at step 0.
Boundary/region labels are noticeably smaller relative to the figure than the source's large italic serif annotations, weakening the label hierarchy.

Apply step 1's state on load (or change step 1's state to the split view) so the narration and the rendered figure agree at the default view.
